purpose: Assigned values for the 8-bit profile_id field as it appears in TRANSPORT_OFFER and TRANSPORT_ACCEPT for the BLE binding. Profile identifiers are transport-scoped: profile 1 under BLE and profile 1 under IP are unrelated assignments and must never be compared.
why_this_exists: Before this registry, every binding's examples used profile_id = 1 with no definition anywhere. Two implementations could agree on transport_id 3 and still be unable to talk, because one meant connectionless advertising and the other meant connected GATT with a particular MTU assumption.
A convention that fossilises is worse than an absent one: once shipping code assumes profile 1 means whatever it happens to do, the value cannot be defined later without breaking it.

allocation_policy.0x00: Reserved. Never assigned, so an uninitialised field names no profile.

profiles.name: RESERVED
profiles.detail: Permanently reserved. An offer carrying profile_id 0 is malformed.

profiles.name: BLE-GATT
profiles.detail: Connected GATT carriage: one MCL Link frame per write, fragmented when the frame exceeds the negotiated ATT payload, with fragmentation defined at the 23-byte minimum ATT MTU because that is the only value every peer must support. Defined normatively by the specification below.

standards_action_record.change_controller: The MCL maintainer, per GOVERNANCE.md section 4.

requirements.mcl_specification_change: mcl-ble/spec/ble-gatt-profile-v1.md moves from Candidate to Stable and names this value normatively. The value is now part of the specification rather than a parameter of the reference implementation.
requirements.architecture_review: profile_id is transport-scoped and 8 bits wide. This assignment changes no Core semantics, adds no field, and consumes one value in the BLE profile space only. Profile 1 under this transport and profile 1 in mcl-ip/registries/ip-profiles-v0.1.json are unrelated assignments and are never compared.
requirements.conformance_implications_documented: profile_id travels inside TRANSPORT_OFFER and TRANSPORT_ACCEPT, so assigning it changes the bytes under test. C4 and C5 are re-run on the final assigned bytes and the major-1 vector family is regenerated before first publication. See the conformance_rerun block.
requirements.collision_redundancy_review: Value 1 was unassigned in this registry. 0 is permanently reserved so an uninitialised field names no profile. No other Standards Action value is assigned here, so there is nothing to collide with and no existing Stable profile this duplicates.

promotion_evidence.step_1_candidate_specification: Complete. The normative specification named above.
promotion_evidence.step_2_independent_implementation: mcl-core/conformance/independent/ -- a clean-room implementation in Python sharing no code, no language and no build system with the reference C. It interoperated on the Experimental Use value 192: test_profiles_c5.py, 60 checks, both directions, matching refusals.
promotion_evidence.step_3_registry_promotion_gate: Satisfied by step 2 together with the specification being complete: the profile parameters are fixed by the document rather than by reference implementation behaviour, which is what the gate asked for.
promotion_evidence.step_5_conformance_rerun_on_final_bytes: C4 and C5 re-run against this assigned value; the major-1 vector family regenerated to carry it.
promotion_evidence.what_this_evidence_is_not: The independent implementation is independent OF THE REFERENCE CODE and was written by the same author. It is strong evidence that these specifications can be read and implemented from the text alone -- it found three real specification-reading defects -- and it is NOT evidence that two organisations have interoperated. v1.0.0 does not claim that. See mcl-core/conformance/ICS.md and V1_SCOPE.md section 5.7.

profiles.over_air_evidence: mcl-ble/evidence/e4-ble-gatt-20260902/ demonstrated this carriage between two machines. That run carried profile_id 192, because this value did not exist yet. It is transport evidence about the carriage -- it does not transfer to these bytes, and the conformance evidence for profile 1 is the C4/C5 re-run recorded below, not this.
profiles.stability: Assigned. Never reused, never redefined. A change to what these bytes mean is a new profile value, not an edit to this row (REGISTRY_POLICY.md rule 7).

profiles.name: BLE-X0-GATT-EXPERIMENTAL
profiles.detail: Connected GATT carriage: one MCL Link frame per write, fragmented per mcl-ble when the frame exceeds the negotiated ATT payload. Fragmentation is exercised at the 23-byte minimum ATT MTU rather than the larger MTU a host may negotiate, because the minimum is the only value every peer must support. Rendezvous beacon in advertising Service Data for the MCL 128-bit service UUID.
profiles.evidence: mcl-ble/evidence/e4-ble-gatt-20260902/ demonstrated this carriage between two machines. That is transport evidence, not a conformance pass: no normative profile exists to conform to.
profiles.promotion_gate: Satisfied and closed on 2026-09-04. The gate asked for a second independent implementation to interoperate on this value with the parameters fixed by specification rather than by the reference implementation; both held, and the Standards Action assignment that followed is profile 1. This value was not promoted -- it stays Experimental Use.
promotion_sequence: 1. Normative specification, complete, at Candidate. DONE.
2. Independent implementation interoperated using this Experimental Use value. DONE -- C5, 60 checks.
4. Standards Action assignment of the final Stable value. DONE on 2026-09-04 -- profile 1.
5. C4/C5 re-run with the final assigned bytes. DONE.
profiles.must_not: Relabel this experimental value as Stable. REGISTRY_POLICY.md is explicit that Experimental Use values are not globally interoperable assignments, and renaming one does not make it one.
profiles.still_experimental: This value remains Experimental Use permanently. It was NOT relabelled: profile 1 is a new assignment in the Standards Action range. Evidence gathered under 192 is evidence about 192, and this row keeps it rather than moving it.

profiles.name: BLE-X1-CONNECTIONLESS-EXPERIMENTAL
profiles.detail: Connectionless carriage: a Link frame small enough for the 31-byte advertising payload is broadcast without a connection. Suitable for presence and hazard, which have no addressee. No fragmentation, so a frame that does not fit is not sendable under this profile.
profiles.evidence: The same evidence record decoded a 19-byte Tier-0 PRESENCE Link frame from a scan response.
profiles.promotion_gate: Open. Requires the same sequence profile 1 completed: an independent implementation interoperating on this experimental value against a normative specification. No such specification is written, so this profile has no promotion path started.

notes: Profile 1 is the Stable assignment and is what an interoperable BLE deployment uses. 192 and 193 remain Experimental Use permanently.

The Experimental values came first deliberately. Until the specification was complete these profiles were defined by reference-implementation behaviour, and an Experimental assignment says so in the value itself. Profile 1 was assigned only once the document, not the code, was the definition -- which is why the value was not simply claimed at the start, when claiming it would have frozen a convention before anything defined it.
A profile_id says nothing about security. A BLE link with a completed pairing is not an authenticated peer; see mcl-core/SECURITY.md.
An implementation receiving an unassigned profile_id MUST NOT guess. It refuses the offer and may continue on its current transport.

governance.change_controller: The MCL maintainer (the owner of the eight MCL repositories).
governance.procedures: mcl-core/governance/GOVERNANCE.md section 4 defines application, review, promotion and deprecation for every MCL registry. They are defined once there rather than restated per registry, so they cannot drift apart.
governance.application: GOVERNANCE.md 4.1 -- an issue naming the registry, requested range, meaning, a permanent specification reference, and the failure behaviour required of a receiver that does not implement it. An application without a specification reference is not an application.
governance.promotion: GOVERNANCE.md 4.3 -- an Experimental Use value is NEVER relabelled Stable. Promotion assigns a NEW value in the Standards Action range after an independent implementation has interoperated using the experimental one, and re-runs conformance evidence on the final assigned bytes.
governance.deprecation: GOVERNANCE.md 4.4 -- a retired assignment becomes a permanent tombstone. Its value is never reused and a decoder must refuse it, because a peer that once meant something by that value would otherwise be misread rather than refused.
